products.name: Lempo
products.description:
Lempo sets every word as if someone inflated it.

Thick, round strokes and soft corners make short words look friendly and loud at once: a café sign, a kids' book cover, a sticker sheet, a sale banner. It reads best big and short, one to five words at a time.

The file has 144 glyphs, including € £ ¥, the fractions ½ ¼ ¾, and © ® ™, so price tags and product labels set without workarounds.

products.name: Nananad
products.description:
Nananad is my 7-year-old daughter's handwriting.

One day I watched her fill a notebook page and saw how neat and expressive her letters were for her age. I wanted to keep that moment, so I turned her handwriting into a font. It is her first creative work.

The letters are not polished, and that is the point. The small wobbles, uneven spacing and playful shapes are all hers. Use Nananad for birthday cards, school projects, children's books and anything that should look like a real child wrote it.

products.name: Morbula
products.description:
Morbula looks like the title of a 1970s sci-fi paperback.

Chunky letters with uneven heights, cut-in notches and squared-off curves make every word look a little strange, in a good way. Set it big on album covers, gig posters, streetwear prints and game titles, where one or two words carry the whole design.

The file has 138 glyphs, including € £ ¥ and © ® ™ for posters, merch tags and price labels.
